review_note: Checked: helper and test read line by line; SHA-256 of test and helper match the receipt; the 6 linked row_keys (Poisson, NB2, Gamma by relmat and by spatial, all intercept SD, q=1, independent) equal the receipt candidate_rows verbatim and each is fitted literally with its own family and log link (Gamma(link='log')). Oracle: b34_laplace() is base R, with hand log densities and first and second eta-derivatives for Poisson, NB2 (size 1/sigma^2) and Gamma (shape 1/sigma^2), a dense joint Newton mode with step halving, Q = chol2inv(K), and the Laplace logLik; no drmTMB code. Evaluated at the live Julia estimates (6 live blocks, skips 0). Agreement with logLik(fit), tolerance 1e-5: Poisson relmat 8.3e-7, spatial 5.1e-7; NB2 relmat 4.0e-7, spatial 4.8e-7; Gamma relmat 1.1e-6, spatial 3.2e-6 (largest, 3.1 x below tol). Bug gaps are all above 20 x tol: selector swap 64 to 573, reversed SD vector 13.7 to 134, kernel by position 15.6 to 106, SD intercept +log 2 3.3 to 10.5, cov2cor(K) 1.0 to 3.3 (relmat), mean-distance range 0.065, 0.140 and 0.0016 (spatial). The smallest gap is NB2 spatial range, 0.0016, 158 x the tolerance but about 3,300 x the observed agreement; the other kernel bugs also discriminate that route (kernel by position 19.6). Shuffled rows, named levels, kernel/coordinates permuted, unique(id) order asserted different; one-step profile check at +-0.1 on mu and SD coefficients passes at 1e-5. The relmat diagonal-spread assertion uses a seed-1 fixture, but K for relmat is deterministic, so it still tests the actual kernel. Console log clean (99 passed, 0 failures, errors, skips, warnings). What this does NOT establish: the oracle is a Laplace approximation of the same kind Julia uses, so it shows the Julia objective is assembled correctly, not that Laplace is close to the exact marginal for these fixtures. No animal route is covered for the count families.
